explanation: Dinosaurs appear in the fossil record about 100 million years before the oldest widely accepted fossils of flowering plants. Early dinosaurs lived among ferns, cycads and conifers, and grasses came later still.

claims.text: The oldest widely accepted dinosaur fossils are about 230 million years old.
The oldest widely accepted flowering plant fossils are about 130 million years old.
Dinosaurs existed for about 100 million years before flowering plants appeared.
Early dinosaurs lived among plants such as ferns, cycads and conifers.
Grasses are a later branch of the flowering plants.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: five listed; c1 to c3 hold numbers, so they are high. c3 is arithmetic on c1 and c2 (230 minus 130 is 100 million years), so a calculation entry can confirm it once they are confirmed. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology, so none applies and every high-risk claim needs web evidence from checker A. rivalTest: the dinosaur-among-flowers picture is the planted trap. Margin: even disputed claims of older flowers, at about 160 to 175 million years, are far younger than the first dinosaurs, so the order holds under every date on offer. volatility: slow: 'oldest widely accepted fossils' is a record that a new find can move, as the guide's sharks-and-trees example notes, although no plausible find flips the answer (disputed Triassic pollen claims are not widely accepted). The guide leaves reviewBy null in a draft for the editor to set at acceptance, but the CNT-1 schema refuses a slow item without one, so I entered a placeholder 24 months from drafting; the editor should reset it from the acceptance date, which an accept edit allows because no packet shows the field; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: a global fact with no local knowledge. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 27 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a comparison item. doubts: the displayed values are rounded to the figures most references use; I am confident of the order.
